data.narrative:
Karman Industries is a Seed-stage company in Climate & Energy founded by David Tearse and Chiranjeev Kalra. The target has raised $11.5M to date. The valuation analysis drew on a comp universe of 9 private peers in the Climate & Energy sector, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, alongside 1 public comparable (LNZA).

Stage-progression analysis proved the sole applicable triangulation method. Using total capital raised ($11.5M, rounded to $12M as a valuation proxy) as the base and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the next stage, this method implied a valuation of $29M. A peer-median approach was not viable; while 9 same-sector peers exist, none yielded three or more datapoints when filtered by stage, adjacency, or valuation tier, making a narrow peer comparison unreliable. Applying an all-sector median would have introduced undue noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $24M to $33M, centered on $29M. This range reflects the 2.5x multiplier with conservative and optimistic bounds. Key uncertainties include the absence of early-stage Climate & Energy comparables with recent, validated metrics, limiting confidence in stage-specific step-up assumptions. The company's position within the sector relative to these 9 peers—in terms of technology maturity, capital efficiency, or market opportunity—remains a material variable not captured by this single-method approach.
